# hs-sql-agent

> hs-sql-agent provides governed SQL access for AI agents through MCP, with fail-closed typed SQL compilation, scoped access policies, approval-gated DML, and support for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, SQLite, and Firebird.

Current documented release: **2.0.5**. Product behavior is pinned by `src/data/productRelease.ts`; prerelease documentation may pin an immutable product commit until the matching release tag exists.

The documentation site is localized in English, Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, and German. Prefer stable unversioned documentation URLs for the current release.

## Product consumption paths

- **Standalone service:** deploy the official Docker image / ToolBox composition.
- **Complete embedded product:** use `HsSqlAgent.Hosting` for the standard first-party composition and configuration contract.
- **Custom ASP.NET Core integration:** use `HsSqlAgent.Server` when the host must own authentication, authorization, middleware, UI, telemetry, or approval-provider composition.

## Built-in MCP tools

The built-in surface is intentionally limited to exactly five names:

- `get_schemas`
- `get_tables`
- `get_columns`
- `execute_query_sql`
- `execute_dml_sql`

All five built-ins expose MCP structured results with inferred output schemas. Read/query tools return typed success/error payloads instead of requiring clients to parse presentation text.

`execute_query_sql` returns `Success`, `Provider`, `RowCount`, `DurationMs`, `Rows`, and `Error`.

Metadata discovery is also structured. Table and column results can include authorized Semantic Layer display names, descriptions, synonyms, relationships, and metrics.

`execute_dml_sql` returns an explicit `Status` of `committed`, `pending`, `rejected`, or `failed`. It also exposes `Provider`, `Committed`, `StatementCount`, `AffectedRows`, `ApprovalWaitDurationMs`, `ApprovalDecision`, `ApprovalRequestId`, `ApprovalExternalReference`, `ReturnedRows`, `Message`, and `Error`. `pending` and `rejected` are approval states rather than execution errors; `Error` is populated only when `Status` is `failed`.

DML remains opt-in for newly issued MCP keys. The default posture selects the four read/query tools and excludes `execute_dml_sql`.

Published Custom Tools can extend a database's tool collection but are not additional built-in tools.

## SQL compiler and Safe DML

- [Execution model](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/sql-compiler/execution-model)
- [SQL support](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/sql-compiler/sql-support)
- [Database dialects](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/sql-compiler/database-dialects)
- [Safe DML](https://sql-agent.net/en/docs/sql-compiler/safe-dml)

The structured-result release does not bypass or weaken the typed SQL pipeline. SQL still passes parse, bind, authorization, policy validation, target-capability proof, compilation, and provider execution boundaries.

For `UPDATE` and `DELETE`, approval binds exact row-set evidence and revalidates before mutation. `INSERT ... VALUES` binds immutable payload evidence. Multi-statement DML remains one server-owned atomic transaction; client-supplied transaction-control SQL is rejected.

## DML approval providers

MCP Elicitation remains the default first-party approval provider. The official Webhook adapter and custom `IDmlApprovalProvider` implementations remain available for modular hosting.

An asynchronous provider may return `Pending`. Durable completion remains server-owned and revalidates current authorization, configuration, policy, plan, row-set, and affected-row evidence before commit.
